title.zh: 卷一百二十五 列傳第十二: 賽典赤贍思丁 布魯海牙 高智耀 鐵哥
title.en: Volume 125 Biographies 12: Ajall Shams al-Din Omar, Buluhaiya, Gaozhiyao, Tiege
title.raw: 卷一百二十五 列傳第十二: 賽典赤贍思丁 布魯海牙 高智耀 鐵哥 Volume 125 Biographies 12: Ajall Shams al-Din Omar, Buluhaiya, Gaozhiyao, Tiege

sentences.zh: 賽典赤贍思丁

translations.literal: Ajall Shams al-Din Omar
translations.idiomatic: Ajall Shams al-Din Omar

sentences.zh: 賽典赤贍思丁一名烏馬兒，回回人，別菴伯爾之裔。

translations.literal: Ajall Shams al-Din Omar was also called Umar. He was a Muslim, a descendant of Bukhara.
translations.idiomatic: Sayid Ajall Shams al-Din Omar, also known as Umar, was a Muslim and a scion of the house of Bukhara.

sentences.zh: 其國言賽典赤，猶華言貴族也。

translations.literal: In his country the term Sayid Ajall means the same as the Chinese term for noble.
translations.idiomatic: In his native tongue, sayid ajall meant much the same as “noble” in Chinese.

sentences.zh: 太祖西征，贍思丁率千騎以文豹白鶻迎降，命入宿衛，從征伐，以賽典赤呼之而不名。

translations.literal: When the Taizu campaigned westward, Shams al-Din led a thousand horsemen to submit with patterned leopard skins and white goshawks as tribute. He was ordered into the night guard, followed on campaigns, and was addressed as Sayid Ajall rather than by his personal name.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizu marched west, Shams al-Din came forward with a thousand riders, offering tribute of figured leopard pelts and white goshawks. Taizu enrolled him in the imperial guard and took him on campaign, calling him Sayid Ajall instead of using his name.

sentences.zh: 七年，分鎮四川，宋將昝萬壽擁強兵守嘉定，與賽典赤軍對壘，一以誠意待之，不為侵掠，萬壽心服。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was assigned to garrison Sichuan. The Song general Zan Wanshou held strong forces at Jiading and faced Sayid Ajall’s army across the lines. Sayid Ajall treated him entirely with sincerity and made no raids; Wanshou came to respect him.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was posted to hold Sichuan. The Song commander Zan Wanshou massed a large force at Jiading and stood opposite Sayid Ajall’s troops. Sayid Ajall dealt with him in good faith alone and did not plunder; Wanshou was won over.

sentences.zh: 未幾，賽典赤召還，萬壽請置酒為好，左右皆難之，賽典赤竟往不疑。

translations.literal: Before long Sayid Ajall was recalled. Wanshou asked to set out wine in friendship. His attendants all objected, yet Sayid Ajall went without hesitation.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward Sayid Ajall was summoned back. Wanshou invited him to a friendly banquet. His staff all urged against it, but Sayid Ajall went anyway without a second thought.

sentences.zh: 酒至，左右復言未可飲，賽典赤笑曰：「若等何見之小耶。

translations.literal: When the wine arrived his attendants again said he must not drink. Sayid Ajall laughed and said, “How petty you are in your outlook.
translations.idiomatic: When the wine was served his men again warned him not to drink. Sayid Ajall laughed and said, “How small-minded you are.

sentences.zh: 咎將軍能毒我，其能盡毒我朝之人乎。

translations.literal: Even if General Zan could poison me, could he poison every man of our dynasty?
translations.idiomatic: Even if General Zan meant to poison me, could he poison every subject of our court?

sentences.zh: 」萬壽嘆服。

translations.literal: ” Wanshou sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: ” Wanshou sighed in deep admiration.

sentences.zh: 八年，有旨：大軍見圍襄陽，各道宜進兵以牽制之。

translations.literal: In the eighth year an edict stated that since the main army was besieging Xiangyang, each route should advance troops to tie down the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year an edict went out: with the main forces investing Xiangyang, every command should move troops to pin the enemy down.

sentences.zh: 於是賽典赤偕鄭鼎率兵水陸並進，至嘉定，獲宋將二人，順流縱筏，斷其浮橋，獲戰艦二十八艘。

translations.literal: Thereupon Sayid Ajall together with Zheng Ding led troops by land and water in concert. Reaching Jiading they captured two Song officers, sent rafts downstream, cut the floating bridge, and took twenty-eight war vessels.
translations.idiomatic: Sayid Ajall then joined Zheng Ding and advanced by land and water together. At Jiading they seized two Song commanders, sent rafts downriver, severed the pontoon bridge, and captured twenty-eight warships.

sentences.zh: 尋命行省事于興元，專給糧餉。

translations.literal: Soon he was ordered to establish a branch secretariat at Xingyuan to supply provisions exclusively.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon ordered to set up a branch secretariat at Xingyuan devoted solely to provisioning.

sentences.zh: 十一年，帝謂賽典赤曰：「雲南朕嘗親臨，比因委任失宜，使遠人不安，欲選謹厚者撫治之，無如卿者。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year the emperor said to Sayid Ajall, “I once went in person to Yunnan. Because appointments there were ill chosen the distant peoples grew restless. I wish to choose a man of careful integrity to pacify them, and there is no one like you.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year the emperor told Sayid Ajall, “I have been to Yunnan myself. Poor appointments have unsettled the frontier peoples, and I want someone steadfast to govern them—no one suits better than you.

sentences.zh: 」賽典赤拜受命，退朝，即訪求知雲南地理者，畫其山川城郭、驛舍軍屯、夷險遠近為圖以進，帝大悅，遂拜平章政事，行省雲南，賜鈔五十萬緡、金寶無筭。

translations.literal: ” Sayid Ajall bowed and accepted the charge. Leaving court he at once sought those who knew Yunnan’s geography, had them map its mountains and rivers, cities and towns, post stations and garrisons, and the distances and dangers of the Yi regions, and presented the chart. The emperor was greatly pleased, appointed him Grand Councillor of State, made him regional commissioner for Yunnan, and granted five hundred thousand strings of paper money and countless gold and treasures.
translations.idiomatic: ” Sayid Ajall bowed and took the commission. After court he immediately found men acquainted with Yunnan’s terrain and had them chart its mountains, rivers, walled towns, relay stations, military colonies, and the routes and hazards of the native districts, then submitted the map. The emperor was delighted, named him Grand Councillor, put him in charge of the Yunnan branch secretariat, and gave him five hundred thousand strings of paper money and untold gold and jewels.

sentences.zh: 時宗王脫忽魯方鎮雲南，惑於左右之言，以賽典赤至，必奪其權，具甲兵以為備。

translations.literal: At that time the imperial prince Tokhughul was stationed in Yunnan. Misled by those around him, he believed that when Sayid Ajall arrived he would surely seize his authority, and he readied armor and weapons in preparation.
translations.idiomatic: The prince Tokhughul was then governing Yunnan. His courtiers persuaded him that Sayid Ajall’s arrival would strip him of power, and he armed his troops in precaution.

sentences.zh: 賽典赤聞之，乃遣其子納速剌丁先至王所，請曰：「天子以雲南守者非人，致諸國背叛，故命臣來安集之，且戒以至境即加撫循，今未敢專，願王遣一人來共議。

translations.literal: When Sayid Ajall heard this he sent his son Nasir al-Din ahead to the prince’s residence with a request: “The Son of Heaven holds that Yunnan’s guardians were unworthy and made the states rebel, so he has sent me to settle them. He also warned that as soon as I reached the border I must extend comfort. I do not yet dare act alone and ask that Your Highness send one man to deliberate together.
translations.idiomatic: Learning of this, Sayid Ajall sent his son Nasir al-Din ahead to the prince with a message: “The Son of Heaven found Yunnan’s stewards unfit, which drove the peoples to revolt, and has sent me to restore order, charging me to show kindness the moment I cross the border. I dare not decide alone—will Your Highness send someone to counsel with me?”

sentences.zh: 」王聞，遽罵其下曰：「吾幾為汝輩所誤。

translations.literal: ” When the prince heard this he at once rebuked his subordinates, saying, “I was nearly led astray by you lot.
translations.idiomatic: ” The prince, hearing this, immediately scolded his men: “You nearly misled me.

sentences.zh: 」明日，遣親臣撒滿、位哈乃等至，賽典赤問以何禮見，對曰：「吾等與納速剌丁偕來，視猶兄弟也，請用子禮見。

translations.literal: ” The next day he sent close retainers Saman, Weihana, and others. Sayid Ajall asked by what rite they would meet. They replied, “We came together with Nasir al-Din and regard you as a brother; please let us meet you with the rites due a son.
translations.idiomatic: ” The next day he dispatched trusted followers Saman, Weihana, and the rest. Sayid Ajall asked what ceremony they would use. They answered, “We came with Nasir al-Din and look on you as a brother—grant us the courtesy shown a son.”

sentences.zh: 」皆以名馬為贄，拜跪甚恭，觀者大駭。

translations.literal: ” Each presented famous horses as gifts and bowed and knelt with great respect; the onlookers were greatly startled.
translations.idiomatic: ” Each offered renowned horses as tribute and bowed with deep respect, to the astonishment of all who watched.

sentences.zh: 乃設宴陳所賜金寶飲器，酒罷，盡以與之，二人大喜過望。

translations.literal: He then set out a banquet and displayed the gold and treasure drinking vessels he had been given. When the wine was finished he gave them all away; the two men were overjoyed beyond expectation.
translations.idiomatic: He then held a feast and set out the gold and jeweled vessels the court had bestowed. When the drinking ended he gave them everything; the two were elated beyond hope.

sentences.zh: 明日來謝，語之曰：「二君雖為宗王親臣，未有名爵，不可以議國事，欲各授君行省斷事官，以未見王，未敢擅授。

translations.literal: The next day they came to give thanks. He told them, “Though you are close kin of the prince, you have no formal titles and may not discuss state affairs. I wish to appoint each of you a regional adjudicator, but having not yet seen the prince I dare not do so on my own.
translations.idiomatic: Next day they returned to thank him. He said, “You are the prince’s kin but hold no rank and cannot deliberate on government. I mean to make each of you a regional adjudicator, yet until I have seen His Highness I may not appoint you alone.”

sentences.zh: 」令一人還，先稟王，王大悅。

translations.literal: ” He had one return first to report to the prince, who was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: ” He sent one back to inform the prince, who was delighted.

sentences.zh: 由是政令一聽賽典赤所為。

translations.literal: From then on all government orders were left entirely to Sayid Ajall.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter every order of government followed Sayid Ajall’s word alone.

sentences.zh: 十二年，奏：「雲南諸夷未附者尚多，今擬宣慰司兼行元帥府事，並聽行省節制。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he memorialized, “Many Yi of Yunnan are still unsubmitted. It is proposed that the Pacification Commission also hold the marshal’s command and that both answer to the branch secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he reported, “Many Yunnan tribes remain unsubmissive. Let the Pacification Commission also exercise marshal authority, both under the regional secretariat.”

sentences.zh: 」又奏：「哈剌章、雲南壤地均也，而州縣皆以萬戶、千戶主之，宜改置令長。

translations.literal: ” He also reported, “Karajang and Yunnan have equal territory, yet their prefectures and counties are all ruled by myriarchs and chiliarchs; the offices of magistrate and chief should be re-established.
translations.idiomatic: ” He added, “Karajang and Yunnan are alike in extent, but districts are run by myriarchs and chiliarchs—magistrates and prefects ought to be restored.”

sentences.zh: 」並從之。

translations.literal: ” Both proposals were approved.
translations.idiomatic: ” Both were approved.

sentences.zh: 十三年，以所改雲南郡縣上聞。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he reported upward the counties and prefectures reformed in Yunnan.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he submitted the list of reorganized Yunnan commanderies.

sentences.zh: 雲南俗無禮儀，男女往往自相配偶，親死則火之，不為喪祭。

translations.literal: Yunnan custom had no ritual propriety; men and women often paired themselves, and when kin died they burned the bodies and performed no mourning rites.
translations.idiomatic: Local custom lacked ceremony: men and women often took partners freely, and the dead were cremated without funeral observance.

sentences.zh: 無稻桑麻，子弟不知讀書。

translations.literal: There were no grain, mulberry, or hemp crops, and the young did not know how to read.
translations.idiomatic: They grew no grain, mulberry, or hemp, and youths did not study books.

sentences.zh: 賽典赤教之拜跪之節，婚姻行媒，死者為之棺槨奠祭，教民播種，為陂池以備水旱，創建孔子廟、明倫堂，購經史，授學田，由是文風稍興。

translations.literal: Sayid Ajall taught them the etiquette of bowing and kneeling, required go-betweens for marriage, provided coffins and offerings for the dead, taught the people to sow seed, built reservoirs against flood and drought, founded temples to Confucius and halls of moral instruction, purchased classics and histories, and granted fields for schools, whereupon literary culture began to rise slightly.
translations.idiomatic: Sayid Ajall taught bowing and kneeling, required marriage brokers, furnished coffins and sacrifices for the dead, instructed people in sowing, dug ponds against drought and flood, built Confucian temples and halls of moral cultivation, bought the classics, endowed school lands, and a modest literary culture began to stir.

sentences.zh: 雲南民以貝代錢，是時初行鈔法，民不便之，賽典赤為聞于朝，許仍其俗。

translations.literal: The people of Yunnan used cowries in place of coin. At that time paper money was first introduced and the people found it inconvenient; Sayid Ajall reported to the court and permission was given to keep their custom.
translations.idiomatic: Yunnan folk used shells as money. When paper currency was introduced they found it burdensome; Sayid Ajall petitioned the throne and they were allowed to keep their practice.

sentences.zh: 又患山路險遠，盜賊出沒，為行者病，相地置鎮，每鎮設土酋吏一人、百夫長一人，往來者或值劫掠，則罪及之。

translations.literal: He also worried that mountain roads were perilous and far, with bandits appearing and disappearing to plague travelers. He chose sites to set posts; at each post he placed one native clerk and one centurion, and if travelers were robbed the responsible men were punished.
translations.idiomatic: He also feared the mountain tracks—remote and dangerous, with bandits harrying travelers. He surveyed the land and set guard posts, each with a native clerk and a centurion; if a traveler was robbed, those men were held liable.

sentences.zh: 有土吏數輩，怨賽典赤不已，用至京師誣其專僭數事。

translations.literal: Several native clerks bore endless resentment toward Sayid Ajall and went to the capital to accuse him of many acts of usurpation.
translations.idiomatic: Certain native clerks, nursing grievances, traveled to the capital and charged him repeatedly with arrogating authority.

sentences.zh: 帝顧侍臣曰：「賽典赤憂國愛民，朕洞知之，此輩何敢誣告！

translations.literal: The emperor turned to his attendants and said, “Sayid Ajall cares for the state and loves the people; I know this thoroughly. How dare this lot falsely accuse him!
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told his courtiers, “Sayid Ajall serves the realm and cherishes the people—I know it well. How dare these men slander him!”

sentences.zh: 」即命械送賽典赤處治之。

translations.literal: ” He at once ordered them bound and sent to Sayid Ajall for punishment.
translations.idiomatic: ” He immediately had them shackled and sent to Sayid Ajall for disposition.

sentences.zh: 既至，脫其械，且諭之曰：「若曹不知上以便宜命我，故訴我專僭，我今不汝罪，且命汝以官，能竭忠自贖乎？

translations.literal: When they arrived he removed their fetters and admonished them, saying, “You did not know that the emperor empowered me with discretionary authority, so you accused me of usurpation. Today I do not punish you but instead give you office—can you devote loyalty to redeem yourselves?
translations.idiomatic: On their arrival he removed their bonds and said, “You did not know the Son of Heaven granted me discretionary power, hence your charge of arrogation. I will not punish you but will give you posts—will you repay me with loyal service?”

sentences.zh: 」皆叩頭拜謝曰：「某有死罪，平章既生之而又官之，誓以死報。」

translations.literal: ” All kowtowed and thanked him, saying, “We deserved death; though the Grand Councillor spared us and even gave us office, we vow to repay with our lives.”
translations.idiomatic: ” They all kowtowed and said, “We merited death; yet the Grand Councillor spared us and even enfeoffed us—we swear to die in your service.”

sentences.zh: 交趾叛服不常，湖廣省發兵屢征不利，賽典赤遣人諭以逆順禍福，且約為兄弟。

translations.literal: Jiaozhi’s submission wavered; the Huguang secretariat sent troops repeatedly without success. Sayid Ajall sent envoys to instruct them in the consequences of rebellion and loyalty and moreover proposed brotherhood.
translations.idiomatic: Jiaozhi’s allegiance was unstable; Huguang’s armies campaigned again and again without gain. Sayid Ajall sent men to explain the rewards and ruin of defiance and fealty and offered a bond of brotherhood.

sentences.zh: 交趾王大喜，親至雲南，賽典赤郊迎，待以賓禮，遂乞永為藩臣。

translations.literal: The king of Jiaozhi was greatly pleased, came in person to Yunnan, and Sayid Ajall met him in the suburbs with guest rites; he then begged to remain a vassal forever.
translations.idiomatic: The king of Jiaozhi rejoiced, traveled to Yunnan in person, was received by Sayid Ajall outside the city with full guest ceremony, and asked to be a tributary forever.

sentences.zh: 蘿槃甸叛，往征之，有憂色，從者問故，賽典赤曰：「吾非憂出征也，憂汝曹冒鋒鏑，不幸以無辜而死；

translations.literal: When Luopan district rebelled he went to suppress it with a troubled look. His followers asked why; Sayid Ajall said, “It is not the campaign that troubles me but that you may rush into blades and die guiltless;
translations.idiomatic: When Luopan rebelled he marched against it, troubled in expression. Asked why, Sayid Ajall said, “I do not worry about the expedition but that you may throw yourselves on spears and die though innocent;

sentences.zh: 又憂汝曹劫虜平民，使不聊生，及民叛，則又從而征之耳。

translations.literal: I also worry that you may plunder civilians and leave them destitute, and that when the people rebel we must campaign again.
translations.idiomatic: I also fear you will loot common folk and leave them ruined, and when they rise again we must fight once more.”

sentences.zh: 」師次蘿槃城，三日不降，諸將請攻之，賽典赤不可，遣使以理諭之。

translations.literal: ” The army halted at Luopan city. For three days they did not submit; the generals asked to attack but Sayid Ajall refused and sent envoys to persuade them by reason.
translations.idiomatic: ” The force encamped at Luopan. After three days without surrender the officers urged assault; Sayid Ajall refused and sent messengers to reason with them.

sentences.zh: 蘿槃主曰：「謹奉命。

translations.literal: The lord of Luopan said, “I respectfully obey.
translations.idiomatic: The Luopan chief said, “I obey your command.”

sentences.zh: 」越三日又不降，諸將奮勇請進兵，賽典赤又不可。

translations.literal: ” After three more days they still did not submit; the officers eagerly asked to advance and Sayid Ajall again refused.
translations.idiomatic: ” Three days later they still held out; the officers pressed to advance and he again refused.

sentences.zh: 俄而將卒有乘城進攻者，賽典赤大怒，遽鳴金止之，召萬戶叱責之曰：「天子命我安撫雲南，未嘗命以殺戮也。

translations.literal: Presently soldiers scaled the walls to attack; Sayid Ajall was furious, sounded the gong to halt them, and summoned the myriarch to rebuke him: “The Son of Heaven ordered me to pacify Yunnan, not to slaughter.
translations.idiomatic: Soon some soldiers climbed the wall to strike; Sayid Ajall was enraged, rang the gong to stop them, and called the myriarch: “The Son of Heaven charged me to soothe Yunnan, never to butcher.”

sentences.zh: 無主將命而擅攻，於軍法當誅。

translations.literal: To attack without the commander’s order violates military law and merits execution.
translations.idiomatic: To attack without command is a capital offense under martial law.

sentences.zh: 」命左右縛之，諸將叩首，請俟城下之日從事。

translations.literal: ” He ordered attendants to bind him; the officers kowtowed and begged to wait until the city fell.
translations.idiomatic: ” He had him bound; the officers kowtowed and asked to defer punishment until the city was taken.

sentences.zh: 蘿槃主聞之曰：「平章寬仁如此，吾拒命不祥。

translations.literal: The lord of Luopan heard and said, “The Grand Councillor is so generous; to resist him is ill-omened.
translations.idiomatic: The Luopan chief heard this and said, “The Grand Councillor is so merciful; defiance would be unlucky.”

sentences.zh: 」乃舉國出降。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon the whole state surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: ” The whole territory then submitted.

sentences.zh: 將卒亦釋不誅。

translations.literal: The soldiers were also released without punishment.
translations.idiomatic: The troops too were spared punishment.

sentences.zh: 由是西南諸夷翕然款附。

translations.literal: From this the Yi of the southwest submitted in concert.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter the southwestern tribes submitted as one.

sentences.zh: 夷酋每來見，例有所獻納，賽典赤悉分賜從官，或以給貧民，秋毫無所私；

translations.literal: When Yi chiefs came to audience they customarily brought gifts; Sayid Ajall divided them among his followers or gave them to the poor, keeping nothing for himself;
translations.idiomatic: Whenever tribal chiefs visited they brought tribute; Sayid Ajall shared it among his staff or the needy, keeping nothing private;

sentences.zh: 為酒食勞酋長，製衣冠襪履，易其卉服草履。

translations.literal: he feasted the chiefs with food and wine, made caps, robes, stockings, and shoes, and replaced their wild dress and grass sandals.
translations.idiomatic: he entertained them with food and drink, furnished caps, robes, hose, and shoes, and exchanged their rustic garb and straw sandals.

sentences.zh: 酋皆感悅。

translations.literal: The chiefs were all moved and pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The chiefs were deeply moved.

sentences.zh: 子五人：長納速剌丁；

translations.literal: He had five sons: the eldest Nasir al-Din;
translations.idiomatic: He had five sons: the eldest, Nasir al-Din;

sentences.zh: 次哈散，廣東道宣慰使都元帥；

translations.literal: the second Hasan, Pacification Commissioner and Marshal of the Guangdong Circuit;
translations.idiomatic: the second, Hasan, Pacification Commissioner and Marshal of Guangdong;

sentences.zh: 次忽辛；

translations.literal: the third Huxin;
translations.idiomatic: the third, Huxin;

sentences.zh: 次苫速丁兀默里，建昌路緫管；

translations.literal: the fourth Shams al-Din Umarli, Commissioner of Jianchang Circuit;
translations.idiomatic: the fourth, Shams al-Din Umarli, circuit intendant of Jianchang;

sentences.zh: 次馬速忽，雲南諸路行中書省平章政事。

translations.literal: the fifth Masuhu, Grand Councillor of the Yunnan Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: the fifth, Masuhu, Grand Councillor of the Yunnan branch secretariat.

sentences.zh: 納速剌丁，累官中奉大夫、雲南諸路宣慰使都元帥。

translations.literal: Nasir al-Din rose through offices to Palace Attendant of the Second Rank and Pacification Commissioner and Marshal of all Yunnan circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Nasir al-Din rose to Palace Attendant of the Second Rank and Pacification Commissioner and Marshal of all Yunnan routes.

sentences.zh: 至元十六年，遷帥大理，以軍抵金齒、蒲、驃、曲蠟、緬國，招安夷寨三百，籍戶十二萬二百，定租賦，置郵傳，立衛兵，歸以馴象十二入貢，有旨賞金五十兩、衣二襲，麾下士賞銀有差。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Zhiyuan he was transferred to command troops at Dali, marched against Jinchi, Pu, Piao, Quyi, and Burma, pacified three hundred Yi stockades, registered 120,200 households, fixed tax levies, established posts, and raised guards. Returning, he presented twelve tame elephants as tribute. An edict rewarded him with fifty taels of gold and two suits of clothing; his soldiers received silver in graded amounts.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 16 he took command at Dali, led troops against Jinchi, Pu, Piao, Quyi, and Burma, pacified three hundred Yi camps, registered 120,200 households, set taxes, established courier stations, and raised guards. He returned with twelve tame elephants as tribute; an edict granted fifty taels of gold and two suits of robes, with graded silver for his men.

sentences.zh: 會其父贍思丁歿，雲南省臣於諸夷失撫綏之方，世祖憂之，近臣以納速剌丁為言。

translations.literal: When his father Shams al-Din died the Yunnan secretariat lost the method of soothing the Yi, and Shizu was troubled. A close attendant spoke for Nasir al-Din.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died the Yunnan officials lost their way with the tribes, troubling Shizu; a courtier recommended Nasir al-Din.

sentences.zh: 十七年，授資德大夫、雲南行中書省左丞，尋陞右丞。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was appointed Virtuous Grand Master and Left Vice Councillor of the Yunnan Branch Secretariat, soon promoted to Right Vice Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he was made Virtuous Grand Master and Left Vice Councillor of the Yunnan secretariat, then Right Vice Councillor.

sentences.zh: 建言三事：其一謂雲南省規措所造金簿貿易病民，宜罷；

translations.literal: He offered three proposals: first, that the gold ledgers the Yunnan secretariat devised for trade harmed the people and should be abolished;
translations.idiomatic: He submitted three proposals: first, that Yunnan’s gold-account trade schemes injured the people and should end;

sentences.zh: 其一謂雲南有省，有宣慰司，又有都元帥府，近宣慰司已奏罷，而元帥府尚存，臣謂行省既兼領軍民，則元帥府亦在所當罷；

translations.literal: second, that Yunnan had a secretariat, a Pacification Commission, and also a Marshal’s headquarters; the Pacification Commission had lately been abolished on memorial, yet the marshal’s office remained—he held that since the secretariat already commanded civil and military affairs, the marshal’s office should likewise be abolished;
translations.idiomatic: second, that Yunnan had a secretariat and Pacification Commission and still a marshal’s headquarters; though the Pacification Commission was lately abolished, the marshal remained—since the secretariat already held civil and military authority, the marshal should go;

sentences.zh: 其一謂雲南官員子弟入質，臣謂達官子弟當遣，餘宜罷。

translations.literal: third, that sons of Yunnan officials were sent as hostages—he held that sons of high officers should be sent but the rest should cease.
translations.idiomatic: third, that officials’ sons were sent as hostages—only sons of ranking officers need go, the rest should stop.

sentences.zh: 奏可。

translations.literal: The memorials were approved.
translations.idiomatic: All were approved.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，進榮祿大夫、平章政事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was promoted to Honored Grand Master and Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he advanced to Honored Grand Master and Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 奏減合剌章冗官，歲省俸金九百餘兩；

translations.literal: He memorialized to reduce redundant Karajang offices, saving more than nine hundred taels of salary gold yearly;
translations.idiomatic: He reported cutting redundant Karajang posts, saving over nine hundred taels of salary gold a year;

sentences.zh: 屯田課程專人掌之，歲得五千兩。

translations.literal: he put garrison farmland revenues under dedicated managers, yielding five thousand taels yearly.
translations.idiomatic: he assigned garrison farmland revenues to dedicated managers, gaining five thousand taels annually.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，以合剌章蒙古軍千人，從皇太子脫歡征交趾，論功賞銀二千兩。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year one thousand Karajang Mongol troops followed Crown Prince Togan in the Jiaozhi campaign; for merit he was rewarded two thousand taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year a thousand Karajang Mongol troops followed Crown Prince Togan against Jiaozhi; he was rewarded two thousand taels of silver for service.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，進拜陝西行省平章政事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he was promoted Grand Councillor of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year he became Grand Councillor of the Shaanxi branch secretariat.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，以疾卒。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he died of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year he died of illness.

sentences.zh: 贈推誠佐理協德功臣、太師、開府儀同三司、上柱國、中書左丞相，封延安王。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed Virtuous Minister Assisting Governance, Grand Preceptor, Commissioner with credentials equal to the Three Dukes, Upper Pillar of State, Left Chancellor of the Secretariat, and Prince of Yan’an.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made Virtuous Minister Assisting Governance, Grand Preceptor, Commissioner equal to the Three Dukes, Upper Pillar of State, Left Chancellor, and Prince of Yan’an.

sentences.zh: 子十二人：伯顏，中書平章政事；

translations.literal: He had twelve sons: Bayan, Grand Councillor of the Secretariat;
translations.idiomatic: He had twelve sons: Bayan, Secretariat Grand Councillor;

sentences.zh: 烏馬兒，江浙行省平章政事；

translations.literal: Umar, Grand Councillor of the Jiang-Zhe Branch Secretariat;
translations.idiomatic: Umar, Grand Councillor of Jiang-Zhe;

sentences.zh: 劄法兒，荊湖宣慰使；

translations.literal: Zhafaer, Pacification Commissioner of Jing-Hu;
translations.idiomatic: Zhafaer, Pacification Commissioner of Jing-Hu;

sentences.zh: 忽先，雲南行省平章政事；

translations.literal: Huxian, Grand Councillor of the Yunnan Branch Secretariat;
translations.idiomatic: Huxian, Yunnan Grand Councillor;

sentences.zh: 沙的，雲南行省左丞；

translations.literal: Shadi, Left Vice Councillor of the Yunnan Branch Secretariat;
translations.idiomatic: Shadi, Yunnan Left Vice Councillor;

sentences.zh: 阿容，太常禮儀院使；

translations.literal: Arong, Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices;
translations.idiomatic: Arong, Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices;

sentences.zh: 伯顏察兒，中書平章政事，佩金虎符，贈太師、開府儀同三司、上柱國、中書左丞相、奉元王，諡忠憲。

translations.literal: Bayanchaer, Secretariat Grand Councillor bearing the golden tiger tally; posthumously Grand Preceptor, Commissioner equal to the Three Dukes, Upper Pillar of State, Left Chancellor, Prince of Fengyuan, posthumous title Loyal and Lawful.
translations.idiomatic: Bayanchaer, Secretariat Grand Councillor with the golden tiger tally; posthumously Grand Preceptor, equal to the Three Dukes, Upper Pillar, Left Chancellor, Prince of Fengyuan, styled Loyal and Lawful.

sentences.zh: 忽辛，至元初以世臣子備宿衛，世祖善其應對。

translations.literal: Huxin, in the early Zhiyuan years as son of a hereditary minister he served in the night guard; Shizu favored his replies.
translations.idiomatic: Huxin, early in Zhiyuan, served in the guard as a hereditary minister’s son; Shizu liked his answers.

sentences.zh: 至元十四年，授兵部郎中。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Zhiyuan he was appointed Bureau Director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 14 he was made Bureau Director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 明年，出為河南等路宣慰司同知。

translations.literal: The next year he went out as Vice Pacification Commissioner of the Henan and other circuits.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he became Vice Pacification Commissioner of Henan and neighboring circuits.

sentences.zh: 河南多強盜，往往群聚山林，劫殺行路，官軍收捕失利，忽辛以招安自任，遣土豪持檄諭之。

translations.literal: Henan had many powerful bandits who often gathered in mountain forests to rob travelers on the roads; government troops failed in pursuit. Huxin took winning them by persuasion as his task and sent local magnates with proclamations to instruct them.
translations.idiomatic: Henan abounded in fierce bandits who clustered in hills and preyed on the highways; official troops could not suppress them. Huxin undertook to win them by persuasion and sent local leaders with edicts to admonish them.

sentences.zh: 未幾，賊二人來自歸，忽辛賜之冠巾，且諭之曰：「汝昔為賊，今既自歸，即良民矣。

translations.literal: Before long two bandits came of their own accord to submit. Huxin gave them caps and scarves and told them, “You were bandits before; now that you have submitted you are good citizens.
translations.idiomatic: Soon two brigands surrendered voluntarily. Huxin gave them caps and scarves and said, “You were outlaws; having submitted, you are lawful subjects.

sentences.zh: 」俾侍左右，出入房闥無間，悉放還，令遍諭其黨。

translations.literal: ” He had them wait on him left and right, entering his private chambers without restriction, then released them all to announce this throughout their bands.
translations.idiomatic: ” He kept them at his side, admitting them to his inner rooms without reserve, then sent them back to spread the word among their fellows.

sentences.zh: 數日後，招集其為首者十輩來，身長各七尺餘，羅拜庭下，顧視異常，衆悉驚怖失措。

translations.literal: Days later he summoned ten ringleaders; each stood over seven feet, bowed in ranks in the courtyard, and looked extraordinary; the crowd was terrified and at a loss.
translations.idiomatic: Within days he gathered ten chiefs; each stood more than seven feet, bowed in the court in ranks, and looked fearsome—the assembly was panic-stricken.

sentences.zh: 忽辛命吏籍其姓名為民，俾隨侍左右，夜則令卧戶外，時呼而飲食之，各得其歡心。

translations.literal: Huxin ordered clerks to register their names as civilians and had them attend him; at night they slept outside his door; he called them to eat and drink and won each man’s heart.
translations.idiomatic: Huxin had clerks enroll their names as commoners and kept them in attendance; at night they slept outside his door; he summoned them to meals and won their goodwill.

sentences.zh: 群盜聞之，相繼款附。

translations.literal: Hearing this, bandit bands submitted one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, outlaw bands surrendered in succession.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，授雲南諸路轉運使。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was appointed Transport Commissioner of all Yunnan routes.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he was made Transport Commissioner of all Yunnan routes.

sentences.zh: 明年，轉陝西道。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to the Shaanxi circuit.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he moved to the Shaanxi circuit.

sentences.zh: 又明年，授燕南河北道宣慰司同知，尋除南京緫管。

translations.literal: The year after he was Vice Pacification Commissioner of the Yan-Nan and Hebei-North circuit, then Nanjing metropolitan intendant.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was Vice Pacification Commissioner of Yan-Nan and Hebei-North, then metropolitan intendant of Nanjing.

sentences.zh: 三十年，授兩浙鹽運使。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year he was Salt Transport Commissioner of the Two Zhe circuits.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirtieth year he became Salt Transport Commissioner of the Two Zhe.

sentences.zh: 大德九年，進江東道宣慰使，改陝西行臺御史中丞，再改雲南行省右丞。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Dade he was promoted Pacification Commissioner of the Jiang-East circuit, then Censor-in-Chief of the Shaanxi Branch Censorate, then Right Vice Councillor of the Yunnan Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In Dade 9 he rose to Pacification Commissioner of Jiang-East, then Censor-in-Chief of the Shaanxi branch censorate, then Right Vice Councillor of Yunnan.

sentences.zh: 既至，條具諸不便事言于宗王，請更張之，王不可，忽辛與左丞劉正馳還京師，有旨令宗王協力施行。

translations.literal: On arrival he listed every harmful practice and reported to the imperial prince, asking reform; the prince refused. Huxin and Left Vice Councillor Liu Zheng rode posthaste to the capital; an edict ordered the prince to cooperate in carrying the measures out.
translations.idiomatic: On reaching Yunnan he catalogued abuses and petitioned the prince for reform; the prince refused. Huxin and Left Vice Councillor Liu Zheng galloped to the capital; an edict commanded the prince to implement the changes jointly.

sentences.zh: 由是一切病民之政，悉革而新之。

translations.literal: Thereupon every policy that harmed the people was abolished and renewed.
translations.idiomatic: Every policy injuring the people was then abolished and replaced.

sentences.zh: 豪民規避徭役，往往投充王府宿衛，有司不勝供給，忽辛按朝廷元額所無者，悉籍為民，去其宿衛三分之二。

translations.literal: Wealthy men often evaded corvée by enrolling as palace guards of the princely house; the offices could not sustain the cost. Huxin registered as commoners all not on the court’s original rolls and removed two-thirds of the guard enrollments.
translations.idiomatic: Rich men dodged labor by enrolling as the prince’s palace guards; officials could not supply them. Huxin enrolled as civilians everyone absent from the court’s original quotas and cut guard service by two-thirds.

sentences.zh: 馬龍州酋謀叛，陰與外賊通，持所受宣敕納賊以示信，事覺，宗王為左右所蔽，將釋不問，忽辛與劉正反覆研鞫，反狀盡得，竟斬之。

translations.literal: The Malong tribal chief plotted rebellion, secretly contacting outside bandits and handing over his commission as proof of trust. When the plot was exposed the prince was shielded by his attendants and meant to release him; Huxin and Liu Zheng examined the case repeatedly until the treason was fully proved and he was executed in the end.
translations.idiomatic: The Malong chieftain plotted revolt, secretly dealing with outside raiders and giving his patent to the enemy as pledge. When discovered the prince’s courtiers would have freed him; Huxin and Liu Zheng investigated until treason was fully established and he was beheaded.

sentences.zh: 軍糧支給，地理遠近不同，吏夤緣為姦，忽辛籍軍戶姓名及倉廩處所，為更番支給，吏姦始除。

translations.literal: Army grain was issued according to distance, and clerks exploited the differences for fraud. Huxin registered household names of soldiers and storehouse locations and arranged rotation of payment, ending clerical abuse.
translations.idiomatic: Army rations varied with distance and clerks profited from the gaps. Huxin registered soldier households and granary sites and instituted rotating issue, ending their fraud.

sentences.zh: 先是，贍思丁為雲南平章時，建孔子廟為學校，撥田五頃，以供祭祀教養。

translations.literal: Previously, when Shams al-Din was Grand Councillor in Yunnan he built a Confucian temple as a school and allotted five qing of fields for sacrifice and instruction.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Shams al-Din served as Yunnan Grand Councillor, he founded a Confucian temple as a school and set aside five qing of land for rites and teaching.

sentences.zh: 贍思丁卒，田為大德寺所有，忽辛按廟學舊籍奪歸之。

translations.literal: When Shams al-Din died the fields passed to the Dade Monastery. Huxin searched the temple-school registers and reclaimed them.
translations.idiomatic: After Shams al-Din’s death the land fell to Dade Monastery; Huxin traced the temple-school records and took it back.

sentences.zh: 乃復下諸郡邑遍立廟學，選文學之士為之教官，文風大興。

translations.literal: He then ordered every prefecture and county to establish temple-schools broadly, chose men of letters as instructors, and literary culture flourished greatly.
translations.idiomatic: He then had temple-schools set up throughout the districts, appointed literati as teachers, and learning flourished.

sentences.zh: 王府畜馬繁多，悉縱之郊，敗民禾稼，而牧人又在民家宿食，室無寧居。

translations.literal: The princely house kept many horses and turned them all loose in the suburbs, ruining the people’s grain; the herdsmen also lodged and ate in common homes so no household had peace.
translations.idiomatic: The prince pastured vast herds in the suburbs, trampling crops, while herders quartered in villagers’ homes and left no house at rest.

sentences.zh: 忽辛度地置草場，搆屋數十間，使為牧所，民得以安。

translations.literal: Huxin surveyed land and set out pasture grounds, built several dozen rooms as herders’ quarters, and the people could live in peace.
translations.idiomatic: Huxin laid out pastures, built dozens of shelters for the herdsmen, and the people found relief.

sentences.zh: 廣南酋沙奴素強悍，宋時嘗賜以金印，雲南諸部悉平，獨此梗化。

translations.literal: The Guangnan chieftain Shanü had always been fierce; the Song once granted him a gold seal. When all Yunnan districts were pacified, only he remained recalcitrant.
translations.idiomatic: The Guangnan chief Shanü was notoriously fierce; the Song had once given him a gold seal. Every Yunnan district submitted except his.

sentences.zh: 忽辛遣使誘致，待之以禮，留數月不遣，酋請還，忽辛曰：「汝欲還，可納印來。

translations.literal: Huxin sent envoys to entice him and treated him with ceremony, keeping him several months without sending him back. The chief asked to return; Huxin said, “If you wish to return, you may hand over your seal.
translations.idiomatic: Huxin invited him with envoys and honored him, detaining him for months. When the chief asked to leave, Huxin said, “Return if you will—but surrender your seal first.

sentences.zh: 」酋不得已，齎印以納，忽辛置酒宴勞，諷令偕印入覲，帝大悅。

translations.literal: ” The chief had no choice and brought the seal to submit. Huxin set out wine to reward him and hinted that he should enter audience with the seal; the emperor was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: ” Forced to comply, he brought the seal. Huxin feasted him and urged him to present it at court; the emperor was delighted.

sentences.zh: 大德五年，緬國主負固不臣，忽辛遣人諭之曰：「我老賽典赤平章子也，惟先訓是遵，凡官府於汝國所不便事，當一切為汝更之。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Dade the lord of Burma stubbornly refused allegiance. Huxin sent men to instruct him, saying, “I am the old Sayid Ajall’s Grand Councillor’s son and follow our forebears’ teaching. Whatever in your land the government finds inconvenient, I shall change it all for you.
translations.idiomatic: In Dade 5 Burma’s king held out. Huxin sent word: “I am heir to old Sayid Ajall the Grand Councillor and keep his ways. Every policy that burdens your realm I will reform.”

sentences.zh: 」緬國主聞之，遂與使者偕來，獻白象一，且曰：「此象古來所未有，今聖德所致，敢效方物。

translations.literal: ” When the lord of Burma heard this he came with the envoys and presented one white elephant, saying, “This elephant has never existed in antiquity; it comes from present sagely virtue, and I dare offer it as tribute.
translations.idiomatic: ” Hearing this, the king came with the envoys, offering a white elephant and saying, “Such a beast never existed before—it is the Son of Heaven’s virtue; I offer it as tribute.”

sentences.zh: 」既入，帝賜緬國主以世子之號。

translations.literal: ” After he entered, the emperor enfeoffed the lord of Burma with the title of imperial son-in-law.
translations.idiomatic: ” On his arrival the emperor granted Burma’s king the style of imperial son-in-law.

sentences.zh: 烏蠻等租賦，歲發軍徵索乃集，忽辛以利害榜諭諸蠻，不遣一卒，而租賦咸足。

translations.literal: Tribute from the Wuman and others had yearly required troops to collect it by force. Huxin posted notices on benefit and harm to the tribes; without sending a single soldier all rents were paid in full.
translations.idiomatic: Wuman and other tribes had paid tribute only when troops forced collection. Huxin posted notices on costs and benefits; without a single soldier all dues were met.

sentences.zh: 俄有為飛語及符讖以惑宗王者，忽辛引劉正密為奏馳報，朝廷遣使臨問，凡造言之徒悉誅之，忽辛偕使者還覲。

translations.literal: Soon slanders and prognostications deluded the prince. Huxin had Liu Zheng secretly memorialize and ride posthaste to report. The court sent envoys to investigate; all who spread rumors were executed. Huxin returned with the envoys to audience.
translations.idiomatic: Rumors and omens then misled the prince. Huxin and Liu Zheng secretly memorialized; the court investigated and executed the rumormongers. Huxin returned with the envoys to audience.

sentences.zh: 大德八年，出為四川行省左丞，改江浙行省。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Dade he went out as Left Vice Councillor of the Sichuan Branch Secretariat, then was transferred to Jiang-Zhe.
translations.idiomatic: In Dade 8 he became Left Vice Councillor of Sichuan, then moved to Jiang-Zhe.

sentences.zh: 至大元年，拜榮祿大夫、江西行省平章政事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhida he was appointed Honored Grand Master and Grand Councillor of the Jiangxi Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhida 1 he was made Honored Grand Master and Grand Councillor of Jiangxi.

sentences.zh: 明年，以母老謝職歸養。

translations.literal: The next year, citing his mother’s age, he resigned to care for her.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he resigned to nurse his aged mother.

sentences.zh: 又明年正月卒。

translations.literal: The next year, in the first month, he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died the following first month.

sentences.zh: 天曆元年，贈守德宣惠敏政功臣、上柱國、雍國公，諡忠簡。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tiansli he was posthumously enfeoffed Loyal and Frugal Minister Upholding Virtue and Fostering Governance, Upper Pillar of State, Duke of Yong, posthumous title Loyal and Simple.
translations.idiomatic: In Tiansli 1 he was posthumously made Loyal Minister Upholding Virtue, Upper Pillar, Duke of Yong, styled Loyal and Simple.

sentences.zh: 子二人：伯杭，中慶路達魯花赤；

translations.literal: He had two sons: Bohang, darughachi of Zhongqing Circuit;
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Bohang, darughachi of Zhongqing;

sentences.zh: 曲列，湖南道宣慰使。

translations.literal: Qulie, Pacification Commissioner of the Hunan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Qulie, Pacification Commissioner of Hunan.

sentences.zh: 布魯海牙

translations.literal: Buluhaiya
translations.idiomatic: Buluhaiya

sentences.zh: 布魯海牙，畏吾人也。

translations.literal: Buluhaiya was a Uighur.
translations.idiomatic: Buluhaiya was a Uighur.

sentences.zh: 祖牙兒八海牙，父吉臺海牙，俱以功為其國世臣。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yarighabaiya and father Jitaihaiya were both hereditary ministers of their state for merit.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yarighabaiya and father Jitaihaiya were hereditary ministers of their realm for service.

sentences.zh: 布魯海牙幼孤，依舅氏家就學，未幾，即善其國書，尤精騎射。

translations.literal: Buluhaiya was orphaned young and studied at his uncle’s house; before long he excelled in his national script and was especially skilled in mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he studied with his uncle and soon mastered the Uighur script and excelled at mounted archery.

sentences.zh: 年十八，隨其主內附，充宿衛。

translations.literal: At eighteen he followed his lord in submission and served in the night guard.
translations.idiomatic: At eighteen he followed his lord into allegiance and entered the imperial guard.

sentences.zh: 太祖西征，布魯海牙扈從，不避勞苦，帝嘉其勤，賜以羊馬氈帳，又以居里可汗女石抹氏配之。

translations.literal: When the Taizu campaigned west Buluhaiya attended him and did not shun hardship. The emperor praised his diligence and gave sheep, horses, felt, and tents, and moreover matched him with the daughter of Khan Jüri, Lady Shimo.
translations.idiomatic: On Taizu’s western campaigns Buluhaiya attended him tirelessly; Taizu rewarded him with sheep, horses, felt tents, and gave him Jüri Khan’s daughter Lady Shimo in marriage.

sentences.zh: 太祖崩，諸王來會，選使燕京緫理財幣。

translations.literal: When the Taizu died the princes assembled and chose envoys to Yanjing to oversee finances.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizu’s death the princes met and chose envoys to manage Yanjing’s treasury.

sentences.zh: 使還，莊聖太后聞其廉謹，以名求之於太宗，凡中宮軍民匠戶之在燕京、中山者，悉命統之，又賜以中山店舍園田、民戶二十，授真定路達魯花赤。

translations.literal: On the envoys’ return the Empress Dowager Zhuang heard of his integrity and asked for him by name from Taizong. All palace, military, artisan, and common households in Yanjing and Zhongshan were placed under his command, and he was also given twenty households of shops, gardens, and fields in Zhongshan and appointed darughachi of Zhending Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Returning, Empress Dowager Zhuang heard of his probity and asked Taizong for him by name. He governed all palace, military, and artisan households in Yanjing and Zhongshan, received shops, gardens, and twenty households in Zhongshan, and became darughachi of Zhending.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，拜燕南諸路廉訪使，佩金虎符，賜民戶十。

translations.literal: In the xinmao year he was appointed Surveillance Commissioner of the Yan-South circuits, bearing the golden tiger tally, and ten households were granted.
translations.idiomatic: In xinmao he was made Surveillance Commissioner of Yan-South with the golden tiger tally and ten households.

sentences.zh: 未幾，授斷事官，使職如故。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed adjudicator while his envoy duties remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was also made adjudicator, retaining his envoy post.

sentences.zh: 時斷事官得專生殺，多倚勢作威，而布魯海牙小心謹密，慎於用刑。

translations.literal: At that time adjudicators could decide life and death alone; many relied on power to act fiercely, while Buluhaiya was careful and discreet and cautious in applying punishment.
translations.idiomatic: Adjudicators then held life-and-death power; many bullied others, but Buluhaiya was cautious in sentencing.

sentences.zh: 有民誤毆人死，吏論以重法，其子號泣請代死，布魯海牙戒吏，使擒于市，懼則殺之。

translations.literal: A man by mistake beat another to death; the clerk argued for the heavy statute. His son wailed and begged to die in his stead. Buluhaiya warned the clerk to seize him in the market—if afraid, then execute.
translations.idiomatic: A man accidentally beat someone dead; clerks urged the death penalty. His son begged to die in his place. Buluhaiya told clerks to seize the son in the market and kill him only if he showed fear.

sentences.zh: 既而不懼，乃曰：「誤毆人死，情有可宥，子而能孝，義無可誅。

translations.literal: Presently he was not afraid, and Buluhaiya said, “Beating a man to death by mistake has grounds for pardon; the son’s filial piety has no grounds for execution.
translations.idiomatic: When the son showed no fear, Buluhaiya said, “Accidental killing may be pardoned; filial devotion cannot be punished.

sentences.zh: 」遂併釋之，使出銀以資葬埋，且呼死者家諭之，其人悅從。

translations.literal: ” He then released them both, had silver paid for burial, and summoned the dead man’s family to instruct them; the man obeyed gladly.
translations.idiomatic: ” He freed both, had silver given for burial, and reasoned with the victim’s kin, who accepted gladly.

sentences.zh: 是時法制未定，奴有罪者，主得專殺，布魯海牙知其非法而不能救，嘗出金贖死者數十人。

translations.literal: At that time the legal system was unsettled; if a slave sinned the master could kill him outright. Buluhaiya knew this was unlawful but could not save them and often paid gold to redeem dozens of the condemned.
translations.idiomatic: Law was still unsettled: masters could kill guilty slaves outright. Buluhaiya knew this was wrong yet often ransomed dozens with his own gold.

sentences.zh: 征討之際，隸軍籍者，憚於行役，往往募人代之，又軍中多逃歸者，朝廷下制：募代者杖百，逃歸者死。

translations.literal: During campaigns those on military registers feared corvée and often hired substitutes; many also deserted from the army. The court decreed: substitutes were flogged one hundred strokes, deserters were executed.
translations.idiomatic: On campaign, registered soldiers hired substitutes or deserted. The court decreed: substitutes flogged a hundred strokes, deserters executed.

sentences.zh: 命布魯海牙與斷事官卜只兒按順天等路，及至州縣，得募人代者萬一千戶、逃者十二人。

translations.literal: Buluhaiya was ordered with adjudicator Bozhier to investigate Shuntian and other circuits. Reaching prefectures and counties they found eleven thousand substitute households and twelve deserters.
translations.idiomatic: Buluhaiya and adjudicator Bozhier inspected Shuntian and other routes, finding eleven thousand substitute households and twelve deserters.

sentences.zh: 然募者聞命將下，已潛遣家人易代募者，布魯海牙聞之，歎曰：「募者已懼罪往易，逃者因單弱思歸，情皆可矜，吾可不伸理耶。

translations.literal: Yet substitutes, hearing the order would descend, had secretly sent kin to replace the hired men; deserters, being few and weak, wished to return—Buluhaiya sighed and said, “Substitutes already fear punishment and change men; deserters, few and weak, yearn to return—the feelings may be pitied; can I not plead for them?
translations.idiomatic: Substitutes, fearing punishment, had kin take their place; deserters were few and weak—Buluhaiya sighed, “Both cases deserve mercy; must I not plead?”

sentences.zh: 」遂奏其狀，皆得輕減。

translations.literal: ” He then reported the facts and all punishments were lightened.
translations.idiomatic: ” He memorialized and all sentences were reduced.

sentences.zh: 有丁多產富而家人不往，及未至役所而即逃者，則曰：「此而不殺，何以戒後！

translations.literal: Where households were numerous and wealthy yet kin did not go, or men fled before reaching service, he said, “If these are not killed, how can later men be warned!
translations.idiomatic: Where rich households sent no one, or men fled before service, he said, “Without death how will others heed?”

sentences.zh: 」有竊妓逃者，吏論當死，布魯海牙曰：「敗亂綱常，罪固宜死；

translations.literal: ” There was one who stole a courtesan and fled; the clerk argued death. Buluhaiya said, “To ruin moral order deserves death;
translations.idiomatic: A man stole a courtesan and fled; clerks sought execution. Buluhaiya said, “Ruining moral order merits death;

sentences.zh: 此妓也，豈可例論！

translations.literal: but this is a courtesan—how can the same rule apply!
translations.idiomatic: yet she is a courtesan—how apply the same rule!”

sentences.zh: 」命杖之。

translations.literal: ” He ordered flogging.
translations.idiomatic: ” He ordered a flogging.

sentences.zh: 其執法平允類如此。

translations.literal: His fair enforcement was mostly of this kind.
translations.idiomatic: His equitable judgments were generally of this sort.

sentences.zh: 布魯海牙性孝友，造大宅於燕京，自畏吾國迎母來居，事之，得祿不入私室。

translations.literal: Buluhaiya was filial and friendly. He built a great house in Yanjing and brought his mother from the Uighur lands to live there, serving her and never putting his salary in his private rooms.
translations.idiomatic: Filial and cordial, he built a mansion in Yanjing and brought his mother from the Uighur country; he never kept his salary for himself.

sentences.zh: 幼時叔父阿里普海牙欺之，盡有其產，及貴顯，築室宅旁，迎阿里普海牙居之，弟益特思海牙以宿憾為言，常慰諭之，終無間言。

translations.literal: In youth his uncle Alipuhaiya had cheated him and taken all his property. When he rose high he built a house beside his uncle’s dwelling and welcomed Alipuhaiya to live there. His brother Yitesihaiya spoke of old resentment, but he always comforted him and in the end there was no estrangement.
translations.idiomatic: His uncle Alipuhaiya had seized his inheritance in youth; in high office he built beside the uncle’s home and welcomed him to live there, soothing his brother’s grievances until harmony prevailed.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗賜以太府綾絹五千匹，絲絮相等，弟求四之一納其國賦，盡與之，無吝色。

translations.literal: The emperor once gave him five thousand bolts of palace silk and an equal amount of floss; his brother asked for a quarter to pay their state tribute, and he gave it all without stint.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once gave five thousand bolts of palace silk and matching floss; his brother asked a quarter for state tribute and he gave it without reluctance.

sentences.zh: 初布魯海牙拜廉使，命下之日，子希憲適生，喜曰：「吾聞古以官為姓，天其以廉為吾宗之姓乎！

translations.literal: When Buluhaiya first received appointment as surveillance commissioner, on the day the order arrived his son Xixian was born. He rejoiced and said, “I hear that in antiquity men took office as surname—perhaps Heaven would make Lian our clan’s surname!
translations.idiomatic: On the day of his surveillance appointment his son Xixian was born. He said, “Ancient men took office as surname—perhaps Heaven makes Lian our clan name!”

sentences.zh: 」故子孫皆姓廉氏。

translations.literal: ” Hence descendants all bear the surname Lian.
translations.idiomatic: ” His descendants all bear the surname Lian.

sentences.zh: 後或奏廉氏仕進者多，宜稍汰去，世祖曰：「布魯海牙功多，子孫亦朕所知，非汝當預。

translations.literal: Later someone memorialized that many of the Lian clan held office and they should be thinned. Shizu said, “Buluhaiya’s merit is great and his descendants are known to me—it is not for you to interfere.
translations.idiomatic: Later a memorial urged thinning the many Lian officials. Shizu said, “Buluhaiya’s service was great; his kin are known to me—not your concern.”

sentences.zh: 」大德初，贈儀同三司、大司徒，追封魏國公，諡孝懿。

translations.literal: In the early Dade years he was posthumously made Commissioner equal to the Three Dukes and Grand Minister of Agriculture, enfeoffed Duke of Wei, posthumous title Filial and Admirable.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Dade he was posthumously Commissioner equal to the Three Dukes, Grand Minister of Agriculture, Duke of Wei, styled Filial and Admirable.

sentences.zh: 子希閔、希憲、希恕、希尹、希顏、希愿、希魯、希貢、希中、希括，孫五十三人，登顯仕者代有之，希憲自有傳。

translations.literal: His sons were Ximin, Xixian, Xishu, Xiyin, Xiyan, Xiyuan, Xilu, Xigong, Xizhong, and Xikuo; fifty-three grandsons, with eminent office in every generation; Xixian has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Sons Ximin, Xixian, Xishu, Xiyin, Xiyan, Xiyuan, Xilu, Xigong, Xizhong, Xikuo; fifty-three grandsons held high office in turn; Xixian has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 高智耀子睿附

translations.literal: Gaozhiyao; son Rui appended
translations.idiomatic: Gaozhiyao; biography of son Rui appended

sentences.zh: 高智耀，河西人，世仕夏國。

translations.literal: Gaozhiyao was a man of Hexi and for generations served the Xia state.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozhiyao of Hexi served the Xia state for generations.

sentences.zh: 曾祖逸，大都督府尹；

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Yi was Director of the Grand Capital Guard;
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Yi was Director of the Grand Capital Guard;

sentences.zh: 祖良惠，右丞相。

translations.literal: his grandfather Lianghui was Right Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: his grandfather Lianghui was Right Chancellor.

sentences.zh: 智耀登本國進士第，夏亡，隱賀蘭山。

translations.literal: Gaozhiyao passed the Xia state’s jinshi examination. When Xia fell he hid on Helan Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozhiyao took the Xia jinshi degree; when Xia fell he hid on Helan Mountain.

sentences.zh: 太宗訪求河西故家子孫之賢者，衆以智耀對，召見將用之，遽辭歸。

translations.literal: Taizong sought worthy descendants of old Hexi families; the multitude named Gaozhiyao. He was summoned for appointment but quickly declined and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong sought worthy scions of Hexi houses; all named Gaozhiyao. Summoned for office, he soon declined and left.

sentences.zh: 皇子闊端鎮西涼，儒者皆隸役，智耀謁藩邸，言儒者給復已久，一旦與冢養同役，非便，請除之。

translations.literal: Prince Kuoduan governed Xiliang; scholars were all subject to corvée. Gaozhiyao visited the princely residence and said scholars had long enjoyed exemption—suddenly to labor like grave keepers was inconvenient and he asked removal.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Kuoduan governed Xiliang; scholars were corvée-bound. Gaozhiyao petitioned the prince: scholars long enjoyed exemption—making them labor like grave tenders was unwise; please release them.

sentences.zh: 皇子從其言。

translations.literal: The prince followed his words.
translations.idiomatic: The prince agreed.

sentences.zh: 欲奏官之，不就。

translations.literal: He wished to memorialize office for him but Gaozhiyao would not accept.
translations.idiomatic: The prince wished to appoint him, but he refused.

sentences.zh: 憲宗即位，智耀入見，言：「儒者所學堯、舜、禹、湯、文、武之道，自古有國家者，用之則治，不用則否，養成其材，將以資其用也。

translations.literal: When Xianzong took the throne Gaozhiyao entered audience and said, “What scholars study is the way of Yao, Shun, Yu, Tang, Wen, and Wu. Since antiquity states that used it were governed; those that did not were not. They are nurtured to supply the state’s use.
translations.idiomatic: At Xianzong’s accession Gaozhiyao said, “Scholars study the way of Yao through Wu; states that employ them prosper, those that do not fail. They are cultivated for the realm’s use.

sentences.zh: 宜蠲免徭役以教育之。

translations.literal: Corvée should be exempted to educate them.
translations.idiomatic: Exempt their corvée to educate them.”

sentences.zh: 」帝問：「儒家何如巫醫？

translations.literal: The emperor asked, “How do Confucians compare to shamans and physicians?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, “How do Confucians compare to shamans and doctors?”

sentences.zh: 」對曰：「儒以綱常治天下，豈方技所得比。

translations.literal: He replied, “Confucians use moral order to govern the realm—how can they be compared to technical trades.
translations.idiomatic: He answered, “Confucians govern by moral order—how compare them to crafts?”

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「善。

translations.literal: ” The emperor said, “Good.
translations.idiomatic: ” The emperor said, “Well said.

sentences.zh: 前此未有以是告朕者。

translations.literal: None before has told me this.
translations.idiomatic: No one told me this before.”

sentences.zh: 」詔復海內儒士徭役，無有所與。

translations.literal: ” An edict restored corvée exemption for scholars throughout the realm with no exceptions.
translations.idiomatic: An edict restored corvée exemption for all scholars empire-wide.

sentences.zh: 世祖在潛邸已聞其賢，及即位，召見，又力言儒術有補治道，反覆辯論，辭累千百。

translations.literal: Shizu in the heir’s residence had already heard of his worth; on taking the throne he summoned him and again urged that Confucian learning aided governance, debating back and forth in thousands of words.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu, as heir, had heard of him; on enthronement he summoned him and argued at length that Confucian learning aids rule.

sentences.zh: 帝異其言，鑄印授之，命凡免役儒戶，皆從之給公文為左驗。

translations.literal: The emperor marveled at his words, cast a seal, and ordered that all exempt scholar households receive official documents as proof.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu marveled, cast a seal, and ordered exempt scholar households receive official proof.

sentences.zh: 時淮、蜀士遭俘虜者，皆沒為奴，智耀奏言：「以儒為驅，古無有也。

translations.literal: At that time scholars captured in Huai and Shu were all made slaves. Gaozhiyao memorialized, “To drive Confucians as slaves—never was this in antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars captured in Huai and Shu were enslaved. Gaozhiyao said, “Driving Confucians as slaves is unheard of in antiquity.

sentences.zh: 陛下方以古道為治，宜除之，以風厲天下。

translations.literal: Your Majesty now governs by the ancient way and should abolish this to admonish the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty governs by the ancient way—abolish this to instruct the empire.”

sentences.zh: 」帝然之，即拜翰林學士，命循行郡縣區別之，得數千人。

translations.literal: The emperor agreed and at once appointed him Hanlin Academician, ordering him to tour counties and distinguish them, finding several thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed, made him Hanlin Academician, and sent him through the counties to identify several thousand scholars.

sentences.zh: 貴臣或言其詭濫，帝詰之，對曰：「士，譬則金也，金色有淺深，謂之非金不可，才藝有淺深，謂之非士亦不可。

translations.literal: Some great ministers said he was fraudulent. The emperor questioned him; he replied, “Scholars are like gold: gold has lighter and darker hues—one cannot say it is not gold; talent has depth and shallowness—one cannot say they are not scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers called it fraud. Questioned, he said, “Scholars are like gold: color varies—you cannot say it is not gold; talent varies—you cannot say they are not scholars.”

sentences.zh: 」帝悅，更寵賚之。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and favored him still more.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and rewarded him further.

sentences.zh: 智耀又言：「國初庶政草創，綱紀未張，宜倣前代，置御史臺以糾肅官常。

translations.literal: Gaozhiyao also said, “At the founding, many policies were provisional and standards unsettled; following past dynasties, an Imperial Censorate should be established to correct official conduct.
translations.idiomatic: He also urged, “At founding, standards were unsettled; follow past dynasties and establish a Censorate to correct officials.”

sentences.zh: 」至元五年立御史臺，用其議也。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhiyuan the Imperial Censorate was established, adopting his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 5 the Censorate was founded on his advice.

sentences.zh: 擢西夏中興等路提刑按察使。

translations.literal: He was promoted Chief Surveillance Commissioner of Xia’s Zhongxing and other circuits.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Chief Surveillance Commissioner of Zhongxing and other Xia circuits.

sentences.zh: 會西北藩王遣使入朝，謂：「本朝舊俗與漢法異，今留漢地，建都邑城郭，儀文制度，遵用漢法，其故何如？

translations.literal: When northwestern princes sent envoys to court they said, “Our old customs differ from Han law; now we remain in Han lands, build capitals and cities, and follow Han ritual and institutions—why?
translations.idiomatic: Northwestern princes asked at court: “Our customs differ from Han law; why build cities in Han lands and follow Han institutions?”

sentences.zh: 」帝求報聘之使以析其問，智耀入見，請行，帝問所荅，畫一敷對，稱旨，即日遣就道。

translations.literal: The emperor sought a return envoy to answer their questions. Gaozhiyao entered audience and asked to go; the emperor asked his reply and he laid out answers point by point that pleased him; that very day he was sent on the road.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sought a rejoinder; Gaozhiyao volunteered, answered each point to satisfaction, and left the same day.

sentences.zh: 至上京，病卒，帝為之震悼。

translations.literal: Reaching Shangdu he died of illness; the emperor mourned in shock.
translations.idiomatic: At Shangdu he died; the emperor grieved deeply.

sentences.zh: 後贈崇文贊治功臣、金紫光祿大夫、司徒、柱國，追封寧國公，諡文忠。

translations.literal: Later he was posthumously enfeoffed Cultivated Text and Governance Minister, Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon, Grand Minister of Agriculture, Pillar of State, Duke of Ning, posthumous title Cultivated and Loyal.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously: Cultivated Text Minister, Gold Seal Grand Master, Grand Minister of Agriculture, Pillar of State, Duke of Ning, styled Cultivated and Loyal.

sentences.zh: 子睿。

translations.literal: His son was Rui.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Rui.

sentences.zh: 睿，資稟直亮，智耀之北使也，攜之以行。

translations.literal: Rui was upright and bright by nature; when Gaozhiyao went north as envoy he took Rui along.
translations.idiomatic: Rui was upright and bright; Gaozhiyao took him on the northern embassy.

sentences.zh: 及卒，帝問其子安在，近臣以睿見，時年十六。

translations.literal: When he died the emperor asked where his son was; a close attendant presented Rui, then sixteen.
translations.idiomatic: On Gaozhiyao’s death the emperor asked for his son; Rui was presented at sixteen.

sentences.zh: 授符寶郎，出入禁闥，恭謹詳雅。

translations.literal: He was appointed Keeper of Seals and Tallies, entering and leaving the inner palace, respectful, careful, and refined.
translations.idiomatic: He was made Keeper of Seals, moving in the inner palace with refined courtesy.

sentences.zh: 久之，授唐兀衛指揮副使，歷翰林待制、禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: After long service he was appointed Deputy Commander of the Tangut Guard, then Hanlin Attendant, then Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Later Deputy Commander of the Tangut Guard, Hanlin Attendant, and Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 除嘉興路緫管，境內有宿盜，白晝掠民財，捕者積十數輩莫敢近。

translations.literal: He was made metropolitan intendant of Jiaxing Circuit. Within the circuit were old bandits who robbed the people’s wealth by day; over ten bands had been seized yet none dared approach.
translations.idiomatic: As Jiaxing intendant, veteran bandits robbed by daylight; a dozen bands were caught yet none dared near.

sentences.zh: 睿下令，不旬日，生擒之，一郡以寧。

translations.literal: Rui issued an order and within ten days captured them alive; the whole commandery was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Rui ordered capture within ten days; the commandery was pacified.

sentences.zh: 擢江東道提刑按察使，部內草竊陸梁，聲言圍宣城，郡將怯懦，城門不開，睿召責之曰：「寇勢方熾，官先示弱，民何所憑。

translations.literal: He was promoted Chief Surveillance Commissioner of the Jiang-East circuit. Within the circuit grass bandits were unruly and announced they would surround Xuancheng. The commandery general was cowardly and would not open the gates. Rui summoned and rebuked him, saying, “The bandits’ force is just swelling—the official first shows weakness; on what can the people rely?
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Jiang-East Surveillance Commissioner, bandits threatened Xuancheng; the general would not open the gates. Rui rebuked him: “Bandits rise and you show fear—what will the people trust?”

sentences.zh: 」即命密治兵衛，而洞開城門，聽民出入貿易自便。

translations.literal: ” He at once ordered troops quietly prepared while opening the gates wide, letting the people come and go and trade as they pleased.
translations.idiomatic: ” He secretly readied troops yet opened the gates for trade as usual.

sentences.zh: 既而寇以有備，不敢進，遂討平之。

translations.literal: Presently the bandits, seeing preparations, did not advance and were suppressed and pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing preparations, the bandits did not advance and were suppressed.

sentences.zh: 除同僉行樞密院事，遷浙西道肅政廉訪使。

translations.literal: He was made Vice Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs, then Surveillance Commissioner of the Jiang-West circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He became Vice Commissioner of Military Affairs, then Jiang-West Surveillance Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 鹽官州民，有連結黨與，持郡邑短長，其目曰十老，吏莫敢問，睿悉按以法，闔境快之。

translations.literal: In Yanguan Prefecture cliques held the county’s weaknesses; their leaders were called the Ten Elders and clerks dared not inquire. Rui prosecuted them all by law and the whole territory rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: At Yanguan, cliques called the Ten Elders bullied the county; Rui prosecuted them and the region rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 拜江南行臺侍御史，進御史中丞，除淮東道肅政廉訪使。

translations.literal: He was appointed Attendant Censor of the Jiangnan Branch Censorate, promoted Censor-in-Chief, then Surveillance Commissioner of the Huai-East circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was Jiangnan Attendant Censor, Censor-in-Chief, then Huai-East Surveillance Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 盜竊真州庫鈔三萬緡，有司大索，追逮平民數百人，吏因為奸利，睿躬自詳讞而得其情，即縱遣之。

translations.literal: Thirty thousand strings of paper money were stolen from the Zhenzhou treasury; officials searched widely and detained hundreds of commoners while clerks profited. Rui personally examined the case, found the truth, and released them.
translations.idiomatic: Thirty thousand strings were stolen from Zhenzhou; hundreds of commoners were detained while clerks profited. Rui tried the case himself and released them.

sentences.zh: 未幾，果得真盜。

translations.literal: Before long the real thieves were indeed captured.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the true thieves were caught.

sentences.zh: 復拜南臺御史中丞，務持大體，有儒者之風焉。

translations.literal: He was again appointed Censor-in-Chief of the Southern Censorate, upholding broad principles with a scholar’s bearing.
translations.idiomatic: Again Southern Censorate Censor-in-Chief, he upheld broad principles with scholarly bearing.

sentences.zh: 延祐元年卒，年六十有六。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yanyou he died at sixty-six.
translations.idiomatic: In Yanyou 1 he died at sixty-six.

sentences.zh: 累贈推忠佐理功臣、太傅、開府儀同三司、上柱國，追封寧國公，諡貞簡。

translations.literal: He was cumulatively posthumously enfeoffed Loyal Minister Assisting Governance, Grand Preceptor, Commissioner equal to the Three Dukes, Upper Pillar of State, Duke of Ning, posthumous title Upright and Simple.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously: Loyal Minister Assisting Governance, Grand Preceptor, equal to the Three Dukes, Upper Pillar, Duke of Ning, styled Upright and Simple.

sentences.zh: 子納麟，官至太尉、江南諸道行御史臺大夫。

translations.literal: His son Nalin rose to Grand Marshal and Grand Censor of the Jiangnan Branch Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: His son Nalin became Grand Marshal and Grand Censor of the Jiangnan branch censorate.

sentences.zh: 鐵哥，姓伽乃氏，迦葉彌兒人。

translations.literal: Tiege, surname Clan Ganaishi, was a man of Kasmir.
translations.idiomatic: Tiege, of the Ganaishi clan, was from Kashmir.

sentences.zh: 迦葉彌兒者，西域築乾國也。

translations.literal: Kasmir is the Western Region state of Zhugan.
translations.idiomatic: Kashmir was the Western Region realm of Zhugan.

sentences.zh: 父斡脫赤與叔父那摩俱學浮屠氏。

translations.literal: His father Wotuochi and uncle Namo both studied the Buddhist teachings.
translations.idiomatic: His father Wotuochi and uncle Namo were both Buddhist monks.

sentences.zh: 斡脫赤兄弟相謂曰：「世道擾攘，吾國將亡，東北有天子氣，盍往歸之。

translations.literal: Wotuochi and his brother said to each other, “The age is in turmoil and our state will perish. To the northeast there is the aura of a Son of Heaven—why not go submit?
translations.idiomatic: The brothers said, “The world is in chaos and our country will fall. Northeast lies the aura of an emperor—let us submit.”

sentences.zh: 」乃偕入見，太宗禮遇之。

translations.literal: ” They went together to audience and Taizong treated them with courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: ” They went to court together and Taizong received them honorably.

sentences.zh: 定宗師事那摩，以斡脫赤佩金符，奉使省民瘼。

translations.literal: Dingzong honored Namo as teacher and gave Wotuochi the golden tally to tour and report the people’s hardships.
translations.idiomatic: Dingzong made Namo his teacher and gave Wotuochi a gold tally to survey the people’s suffering.

sentences.zh: 憲宗尊那摩為國師，授玉印，緫天下釋教。

translations.literal: Xianzong honored Namo as National Preceptor, granted the jade seal, and put him in charge of all Buddhist teaching.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzong made Namo National Preceptor with a jade seal, head of all Buddhism.

sentences.zh: 斡脫赤亦貴用事，領迦葉彌兒萬戶，奏曰：「迦葉彌兒西陲小國，尚未臣服，請往諭之。

translations.literal: Wotuochi also rose in favor and held office, commanding the Kasmir myriarchy. He memorialized, “Kasmir is a small state on the western border not yet submitted; I ask to go instruct them.
translations.idiomatic: Wotuochi grew powerful, commanding the Kashmir myriarchy, and memorialized: “Kashmir on the western marches is unsubmissive—let me go persuade them.”

sentences.zh: 」詔偕近侍以往。

translations.literal: ” An edict ordered him to go with close attendants.
translations.idiomatic: ” An edict sent him with palace attendants.

sentences.zh: 其國主不從，怒而殺之，帝為發兵誅國主。

translations.literal: The lord of that state would not obey, grew angry, and killed him; the emperor sent troops to execute the lord.
translations.idiomatic: The king refused, killed him in anger, and the emperor sent troops to punish the king.

sentences.zh: 元貞元年封代國公，諡忠遂。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuanzhen he was enfeoffed Duke of Dai, posthumous title Loyal and Accomplished.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanzhen 1 he was posthumously Duke of Dai, styled Loyal and Accomplished.

sentences.zh: 先是，世祖事憲宗甚親愛，後以讒稍疏，國師導世祖宜加敬慎，遂友愛如初。

translations.literal: Previously Shizu had been very close to Xianzong but later, because of slander, grew somewhat distant. The National Preceptor advised Shizu to be more respectful and cautious, and brotherly affection returned as at first.
translations.idiomatic: Shizu had been close to Xianzong but slander estranged them until the National Preceptor urged greater respect and their bond was restored.

sentences.zh: 至是，帝將用鐵哥，曰：「吾以酬國師也。

translations.literal: At this time the emperor was about to employ Tiege and said, “I do this to repay the National Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor would employ Tiege and said, “I repay the National Preceptor thus.”

sentences.zh: 」於是鐵哥年十七，詔擇貴家女妻之，辭曰：「臣母漢人，每欲求漢人女為婦，臣不敢傷母心。

translations.literal: ” Tiege was then seventeen; an edict chose a noble family’s daughter for his wife. He declined, saying, “My mother is Han and has always wished for a Han daughter-in-law; I dare not wound my mother’s heart.
translations.idiomatic: ” Tiege was seventeen; the court chose a noble bride. He declined: “My mother is Han and long wished for a Han daughter-in-law—I cannot grieve her.”

sentences.zh: 」乃為娶冉氏女。

translations.literal: ” He was therefore given the Ran clan’s daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: ” He married a daughter of the Ran clan.

sentences.zh: 久之，命掌饔膳湯藥，日益親密。

translations.literal: After long service he was ordered to manage meals and medicinal broths and grew daily more intimate.
translations.idiomatic: He was put in charge of meals and medicines and grew ever closer to the emperor.

sentences.zh: 至元十六年，鐵哥奏曰：「武臣佩符，古制也。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Zhiyuan Tiege memorialized, “Military officers bearing tallies is ancient custom.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 16 Tiege said, “Military officers bearing tallies is ancient custom.

sentences.zh: 今長民者亦佩符，請省之，以彰武職。

translations.literal: Now civil administrators also bear tallies; I ask that this be reduced to show martial office clearly.
translations.idiomatic: Today civil administrators bear them too—abolish that to honor martial rank.”

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: ” The proposal was followed.
translations.idiomatic: ” It was approved.

sentences.zh: 十七年，進正議大夫、尚膳監。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was promoted to Grand Master of Correct Counsel and Director of the Imperial Kitchen.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he became Grand Master of Correct Counsel and Director of the Imperial Kitchen.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗諭之曰：「朕聞父飲藥，子先嘗之，君飲藥，臣先嘗之。

translations.literal: The emperor once instructed him, “I hear that when a father drinks medicine the son tastes it first; when a ruler drinks medicine the minister tastes it first.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, “When a father takes medicine the son tastes it first; when a ruler takes medicine the minister tastes first.

sentences.zh: 今卿典朕膳，凡飲食湯藥，宜先嘗之。

translations.literal: Now you oversee my meals; all food and medicinal broths should first be tasted by you.
translations.idiomatic: You oversee my meals—taste all food and medicines first.”

sentences.zh: 」又曰：「朕以宿衛士隸卿，其可任使者，疏其才能，朕將用之。

translations.literal: ” He also said, “I place my night guards under you; those fit for missions—list their talents and I will employ them.
translations.idiomatic: ” He added, “My guard is yours—list those fit for service and I will use them.”

sentences.zh: 」詔賜第於大明宮之左，留守段圭言：「逼木局，不便。

translations.literal: ” An edict granted a residence to the left of the Great Bright Palace. The Yanjing intendant Duan Gui said, “It presses on the Timber Bureau and is inconvenient.
translations.idiomatic: ” A residence was granted east of the Great Bright Palace; intendant Duan Gui said it crowded the Timber Bureau.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「俾居近禁闥，以便召使。

translations.literal: ” The emperor said, “Let him dwell near the inner palace for easy summons.
translations.idiomatic: ” The emperor said, “Let him live near the inner palace for easy summons.

sentences.zh: 木局稍隘，又何害焉。」

translations.literal: The Timber Bureau is a bit narrow—what harm is there?”
translations.idiomatic: The bureau is cramped—what matter?”

sentences.zh: 高州人言，州境多野獸害稼，願捕以充貢。

translations.literal: Men of Gaozhou said many wild beasts in the district harmed the crops and wished to hunt them to fill tribute.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozhou men said wild beasts ruined crops and asked to hunt them for tribute.

sentences.zh: 鐵哥曰：「捕獸充貢，徒濟其私耳，且擾民，不可聽。

translations.literal: Tiege said, “Hunting beasts for tribute only serves private gain and moreover disturbs the people—it must not be allowed.
translations.idiomatic: Tiege said, “Hunting for tribute serves private ends and harms the people—do not allow it.”

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: ” The emperor followed this.
translations.idiomatic: ” The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 十九年，遷同知宣徽院事，領尚膳監。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was transferred Vice Director of the Palace Provisions Office while still heading the Imperial Kitchen.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he became Vice Director of the Palace Provisions Office, still heading the Imperial Kitchen.

sentences.zh: 有食尚食餘餅者，帝察知之，怒。

translations.literal: Someone ate leftover cakes from the imperial kitchen; the emperor detected it and was angry.
translations.idiomatic: Someone ate leftover imperial cakes; the emperor learned of it and was furious.

sentences.zh: 鐵哥曰：「失餅之罪在臣，食者何與焉。

translations.literal: Tiege said, “The fault of losing cakes lies with me—what have the eaters to do with it?
translations.idiomatic: Tiege said, “Lost cakes are my fault—why punish the eaters?”

sentences.zh: 」內府食用圓米，鐵哥奏曰：「計粳米一石，僅得圓米四斗，請自今非御用，止給常米。

translations.literal: ” The inner palace used polished rice; Tiege memorialized, “Calculating from one shi of husked rice one gets only four dou of polished rice; from now on except for imperial use give ordinary rice only.
translations.idiomatic: ” The palace used polished rice; Tiege said, “One shi of grain yields only four dou polished—except for imperial use give ordinary rice.”

sentences.zh: 」帝皆善之。

translations.literal: ” The emperor approved both.
translations.idiomatic: ” The emperor approved both.

sentences.zh: 進中奉大夫、司農寺達魯花赤。

translations.literal: He was promoted Palace Attendant of the Second Rank and darughachi of the Ministry of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to Palace Attendant of the Second Rank and darughachi of the Ministry of Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 從獵百杳兒之地，獵人亦不剌金射兔，誤中名駝，駝死，帝怒，命誅之。

translations.literal: Following the hunt at Baixiaoer, the hunter Bulajin shot at a hare and by mistake hit a famous camel; the camel died and the emperor was angry and ordered execution.
translations.idiomatic: On a hunt at Baixiaoer, Bulajin shot a hare, hit a prized camel, and the emperor ordered his death.

sentences.zh: 鐵哥曰：「殺人償畜，刑太重。
