translations.literal: Tiege said, “Killing a man to compensate for livestock—the penalty is too heavy.
translations.idiomatic: Tiege said, “Executing a man for a beast—the penalty is too harsh.”

sentences.zh: 」帝驚曰：「 誤耶，史官必書。

translations.literal: ” The emperor started and said, “A mistake? The historiographers will surely record it.
translations.idiomatic: ” The emperor started: “A mistake? The historians will record it.”

sentences.zh: 」亟釋之。

translations.literal: ” He at once released him.
translations.idiomatic: ” He immediately pardoned him.

sentences.zh: 庾人有盜鑿米者，罪當死。

translations.literal: A granary man stole husked rice and the crime merited death.
translations.idiomatic: A granary clerk stole rice and merited death.

sentences.zh: 鐵哥諫曰：「臣鞫庾人，其母病，盜欲食母耳，請貸之。

translations.literal: Tiege remonstrated, “When I examined the granary man, his mother was ill and he stole rice to feed her—please pardon him.
translations.idiomatic: Tiege pleaded, “He stole to feed his sick mother—pardon him.”

sentences.zh: 」牧人有盜割駝峰者，將誅之。

translations.literal: ” A herdsman cut a camel’s hump and was to be executed.
translations.idiomatic: ” A herdsman cut a camel’s hump and faced execution.

sentences.zh: 鐵哥曰：「生割駝峰，誠忍人也。

translations.literal: Tiege said, “To cut a living camel’s hump is indeed cruel.
translations.idiomatic: Tiege said, “Cutting a living camel’s hump is cruel.

sentences.zh: 然殺之，恐乖陛下仁恕心。

translations.literal: Yet to kill him may run against Your Majesty’s benevolent and forgiving heart.
translations.idiomatic: Yet killing him may wound Your Majesty’s mercy.”

sentences.zh: 」詔皆免死。

translations.literal: ” Edicts pardoned both from death.
translations.idiomatic: ” Edicts spared both.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，進正奉大夫，奏：「司農寺宜陞為大司農司，秩二品，使天下知朝廷重農之意。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was promoted Palace Attendant of the First Rank and memorialized, “The Ministry of Agriculture should be raised to the Grand Ministry of Agriculture, rank 2b, so the realm knows the court values farming.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year he was promoted and memorialized raising the Ministry of Agriculture to Grand Ministry, rank 2b, to show the court honors farming.

sentences.zh: 」制可。

translations.literal: ” The decree was approved.
translations.idiomatic: ” Approved.

sentences.zh: 進資善大夫、司農。

translations.literal: He was promoted Virtuous Grand Master and Minister of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: He became Virtuous Grand Master and Minister of Agriculture.

sentences.zh: 時司農供膳，有司多擾民，鐵哥奏曰：「屯田則備諸物，立供膳司甚便。

translations.literal: At that time the Ministry of Agriculture supplied meals and many offices disturbed the people. Tiege memorialized, “Garrison fields supply all goods; establishing a dedicated meals office would be very convenient.
translations.idiomatic: The ministry supplied meals and harassed the people; Tiege urged a dedicated meals office supplied by garrison fields.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: ” The proposal was followed.
translations.idiomatic: ” It was approved.

sentences.zh: 桓州饑民鬻子女以為食，鐵哥奏以官帑贖之。

translations.literal: In Huanzhou starving people sold sons and daughters for food; Tiege memorialized to redeem them with official funds.
translations.idiomatic: In Huanzhou the starving sold children; Tiege had them redeemed from the treasury.

sentences.zh: 二十四年，從征乃顏，至撒兒都之地，叛王塔不台率兵奄至。

translations.literal: In the twenty-fourth year he followed the campaign against Nayan. Reaching Saierdu, the rebel prince Tabutai led troops in sudden assault.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-fourth year he campaigned against Nayan; at Saierdu rebel prince Tabutai attacked suddenly.

sentences.zh: 鐵哥奏曰：「昔李廣一將耳，尚能以疑退敵，況陛下萬乘之威乎。

translations.literal: Tiege memorialized, “In antiquity Li Guang was but one general yet could still repel the enemy by feigning doubt—how much more the majesty of Your Majesty’s ten thousand chariots!
translations.idiomatic: Tiege said, “Li Guang alone once bluffed an enemy away—how much more Your Majesty’s majesty!”

sentences.zh: 今彼衆我寡，不得地利，當設疑以退之。

translations.literal: Now they are many and we few and lack favorable ground; we should set up a ruse to make them withdraw.
translations.idiomatic: ” “They outnumber us and we lack ground—feign strength to make them retreat.”

sentences.zh: 」於是帝張曲蓋，據胡床，鐵哥從容進酒。

translations.literal: ” Thereupon the emperor spread a curved canopy and sat on a barbarian chair while Tiege calmly advanced wine.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor spread a canopy, sat on a camp chair, and Tiege calmly served wine.

sentences.zh: 塔不台按兵覘伺，懼有伏，遂引去。

translations.literal: Tabutai held his troops and watched, fearing an ambush, and then withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Tabutai watched for ambush, then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 帝以金章宗玉帶賜之。

translations.literal: The emperor gave him the Jin emperor Zhangzong’s jade belt.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor gave him Emperor Zhangzong of Jin’s jade belt.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，進榮祿大夫、中書平章政事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he was promoted Honored Grand Master and Grand Councillor of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year he became Honored Grand Master and Secretariat Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 以病足，聽輿轎入殿門。

translations.literal: Because his feet were ill he was permitted to enter the palace gate in a litter.
translations.idiomatic: Ill in the feet, he was allowed a litter inside the palace gate.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗憶北征事，不能悉記，鐵哥條舉甚詳，帝悅，以金束帶賜之。

translations.literal: The emperor once recalled the northern campaigns but could not remember fully; Tiege listed them in detail and the emperor was pleased and gave him a gold belt.
translations.idiomatic: Recalling northern campaigns vaguely, the emperor was pleased when Tiege detailed them and gave a gold belt.

sentences.zh: 初，詔遣宋新附民種蒲萄於野馬川晃火兒不剌之地，既獻其實，鐵哥以北方多寒，奏歲賜衣服，從之。

translations.literal: Initially an edict had newly submitted Song people plant grapes at Yemachuan Huanghuoer Bula; when fruit was presented Tiege, because the north was very cold, memorialized yearly grants of clothing, and this was followed.
translations.idiomatic: Song subjects had been ordered to plant grapes in the northern cold; when fruit came Tiege memorialized yearly clothing grants, which were approved.

sentences.zh: 成宗即位，以鐵哥先朝舊臣，賜銀一千兩、鈔十萬貫。

translations.literal: When Chengzong took the throne, because Tiege was an old minister of the previous reign, he was given one thousand taels of silver and one hundred thousand strings of paper money.
translations.idiomatic: Chengzong, honoring a former reign’s minister, gave a thousand taels of silver and a hundred thousand strings of paper money.

sentences.zh: 他日，又賜以瑪瑙碗，謂鐵哥曰：「此器先皇所用，朕今賜卿，以卿久侍先皇故也。

translations.literal: Another day he again gave an agate bowl and told Tiege, “This vessel the late emperor used; I now give it to you because you long attended the late emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Another day he gave an agate bowl and said, “The late emperor used this—I give it because you long served him.”

sentences.zh: 」大德元年，加光祿大夫。

translations.literal: ” In the first year of Dade he was made Grand Master of the Glory of Office.
translations.idiomatic: ” In Dade 1 he was made Grand Master of the Glory of Office.

sentences.zh: 三年，乞解機務，從之。

translations.literal: In the third year he begged to leave state affairs and was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he asked to retire and was allowed.

sentences.zh: 仍授平章政事、議中書省事。

translations.literal: He was still appointed Grand Councillor to deliberate on Secretariat affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He remained Grand Councillor to deliberate Secretariat business.

sentences.zh: 時諸王朝見，未有知典故者，帝曰：「惟鐵哥知之，俾專其事，凡廩餼金帛之數，皆遵世祖制詔，自今懷諸王之禮，悉命鐵哥掌之。」

translations.literal: At that time when the princes came to audience none knew ritual precedent. The emperor said, “Only Tiege knows it; let him specialize in this matter. All quantities of grain, fodder, gold, and silk follow Shizu’s regulations and edicts. From now on, all rites for receiving the princes shall be commanded to Tiege.”
translations.idiomatic: When princes attended court none knew ritual; the emperor said, “Only Tiege knows—let him manage princely rites and provisions per Shizu’s regulations.”

sentences.zh: 七年，復拜中書平章政事。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was again appointed Grand Councillor of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was again Secretariat Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 平灤大水，鐵哥奏曰：「散財聚民，古之道也。

translations.literal: Great floods struck Pingluan; Tiege memorialized, “To scatter wealth and gather the people is the ancient way.
translations.idiomatic: Pingluan flooded; Tiege said, “To scatter wealth and gather people is the ancient way.

sentences.zh: 今平灤水災，不加賑恤，民不聊生矣！

translations.literal: Now Pingluan suffers flood disaster yet receives no relief—the people cannot live!
translations.idiomatic: ” “Yet Pingluan gets no relief—the people cannot survive!”

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: ” The proposal was followed.
translations.idiomatic: ” Relief was granted.

sentences.zh: 十年，丁母憂，詔奪情起復。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he mourned his mother; an edict ordered him to resume office without leaving mourning.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year his mother died; an edict recalled him from mourning.

sentences.zh: 遼王脫脫入朝，從者執兵入大明宮，鐵哥劾止之，王懼謝。

translations.literal: The Liao prince Toto entered audience; his followers bore weapons into the Great Bright Palace. Tiege impeached and stopped them; the prince feared and apologized.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Toto of Liao’s followers bore arms into the Great Bright Palace; Tiege stopped them and the prince apologized.

sentences.zh: 從幸縉山，饑民相望，鐵哥輒發廩賑之，既乃陳疏自劾，帝稱善不已。

translations.literal: Following the emperor to Jinyun, hungry people stretched as far as one could see; Tiege opened granaries to relieve them, then submitted a memorial impeaching himself; the emperor praised him without end.
translations.idiomatic: At Jinyun, famine victims lined the road; Tiege opened granaries, then memorialized against himself; the emperor praised him endlessly.

sentences.zh: 武宗即位，賜金一百兩，加金紫光祿大夫，遙授中書右丞相。

translations.literal: When Wuzong took the throne he was given one hundred taels of gold, promoted Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon, and appointed Right Chancellor of the Secretariat in absentia.
translations.idiomatic: Wuzong gave a hundred taels of gold, made him Gold Seal Grand Master, and named him Right Chancellor in absentia.

sentences.zh: 有訴寧遠王闊闊出有逆謀者，命誅之。

translations.literal: Someone accused Prince Kuokuochu of Ningyuan of treason and he was ordered executed.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Kuokuochu of Ningyuan was accused of treason and ordered killed.

sentences.zh: 鐵哥知其誣，廷辨之，由是得釋，徙高麗。

translations.literal: Tiege knew it was false and argued in court; thereby he was released and exiled to Goryeo.
translations.idiomatic: Tiege knew the charge false and argued at court; the prince was spared and exiled to Goryeo.

sentences.zh: 二年，領度支院。

translations.literal: In the second year he headed the Revenue Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he headed the Revenue Bureau.

sentences.zh: 尋賜江州稻田五千畝。

translations.literal: Soon he was granted five thousand mu of paddy fields in Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he received five thousand mu of paddy in Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 子六人：忽察，淮東宣慰使；

translations.literal: He had six sons: Hucha, Pacification Commissioner of Huai-East;
translations.idiomatic: He had six sons: Hucha, Huai-East Pacification Commissioner;

sentences.zh: 平安奴，太平路達魯花赤；

translations.literal: Pingannu, darughachi of Taiping Circuit;
translations.idiomatic: Pingannu, darughachi of Taiping;

sentences.zh: 也識哥，同知山東宣慰司事；

translations.literal: Yeshige, Vice Pacification Commissioner of Shandong;
translations.idiomatic: Yeshige, Vice Pacification Commissioner of Shandong;

sentences.zh: 虎里台，同知真定緫管府事；

translations.literal: Hulitai, Vice Commissioner of Zhending metropolitan government;
translations.idiomatic: Hulitai, Vice Commissioner of Zhending;

sentences.zh: 亦可麻，同知都護府事；

translations.literal: Yekema, Vice Commissioner of the Metropolitan Guard Bureau;
translations.idiomatic: Yekema, Vice Commissioner of the Metropolitan Guard;

sentences.zh: 重喜，隆禧院副使。

translations.literal: Zhongxi, Deputy Director of the Longxi Court.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongxi, Deputy Director of the Longxi Court.

sentences.zh: 孫八人，伯顏，中書平章政事，餘多居宿衛。

translations.literal: He had eight grandsons; Bayan was Grand Councillor of the Secretariat; the rest mostly served in the night guard.
translations.idiomatic: Eight grandsons; Bayan was Secretariat Grand Councillor; most others served in the guard.
